It sells fixed and indexed annuities and life insurance through independent agents and advisers, with several brands such as Midland National, North American and Sammons Institutional Group. Total assets exceed 100 billion dollars. Customers are retirees and savers. B2B2C insurer with limited consumer awareness.

Seaspan is a Vancouver-based containership leasing company, one of the world's largest, owning and chartering a fleet of container vessels to major liner companies such as COSCO, MSC, ONE and Maersk, as well as operating ship management through Seaspan Ship Management. It was part of Atlas Corp, taken private in 2023 by Poseidon, owned by Fairfax and OMERS. Founded 2005. Revenue is long-term time charters, over 2 billion dollars. B2B shipping brand with no consumer awareness.

SMFG India Credit, formerly Fullerton India Credit Company, is an Indian non-banking finance company headquartered in Mumbai, owned by Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, which bought control from Temasek's Fullerton in 2021, took full ownership in 2023 and rebranded it in 2024. It offers secured and unsecured loans for small businesses, vehicles and consumers through a branch network across India. Revenue is lending interest. B2B and consumer lender with moderate awareness, helped by its Japanese bank parent.

Archwest Capital is a real estate finance company based in Irvine, California that provides lending and capital for property investors, focused on loans secured by real estate. Revenue comes from interest and fees on loans. Crunchbase lists about $600 million in total funding, the latest in September 2026, which is likely debt or credit facility financing rather than equity. Private. B2B and specialist lender, little public brand awareness.

B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

about: Digit Insurance, now operating as Go Digit General Insurance, sells general insurance in India, including motor, health, travel, property and commercial policies, mostly through digital channels and partners. Customers are Indian consumers and businesses. Founded in 2016 in Bengaluru by Kamesh Goyal and backed by Fairfax and Sachin Bansal; its parent Go Digit Infoworks Services listed on the NSE and BSE in May 2024. Crunchbase shows about $596 million raised. Moderately known Indian consumer insurance brand.

KreditBee is an Indian digital lending platform offering personal loans, instant credit and credit-related products to young salaried professionals and first-time borrowers through its mobile app, alongside bank and NBFC partners. Based in Bangalore and founded in 2018. Revenue comes from interest and fees. It has raised about $642 million in total funding, with a valuation above $1 billion. Private, with IPO plans reported. Known consumer fintech app in India, with heavy digital advertising.

Customers are real estate investors, with revenue from interest income. Based in Westlake Village, California. Listed on the NYSE (VEL) since 2020. Crunchbase shows $575 million in funding. B2B finance brand, little consumer awareness.

about: JD Digits, previously JD Finance, is the digital technology and financial services arm that spun out of JD.com, providing digital finance, cloud, AI and risk technology services to banks, financial institutions, governments and enterprises, plus consumer finance products. Headquartered in Beijing. Founded in 2013, with major backing from JD.com and investors including state-linked funds. Crunchbase shows about CN¥34 billion in total funding. Private and not listed. Known in China through JD's consumer credit products such as JD Baitiao, but largely B2B.

Integrity Marketing Group is a US distributor of life, health and Medicare insurance and annuities, using a network of partner agencies and call centres. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, it was founded in 2006 and grew by acquiring independent agencies. Revenue comes from carrier commissions. Backed by private equity including Silver Lake and TPG. B2B and agent-facing, with moderate consumer reach via Medicare marketing.

LendingPoint is a US fintech lender based in Kennesaw, Georgia, offering personal loans and point-of-sale financing online to near-prime consumers, using its own credit models. Revenue comes from interest and fees. Founded in 2014. Crunchbase shows about $1.9 billion in funding, mostly debt facilities. Private. Small consumer finance brand.

about: N26 is a Berlin-based mobile bank offering current accounts, debit cards, savings, loans, insurance and investing through its app, serving several million customers in Europe, with a German banking licence. Founded in 2013 by Valentin Stalf and Maximilian Tayenthal. Revenue comes from card interchange, subscriptions and lending, and it has been valued at over $9 billion at its peak. Private. Well-known European neobank, with substantial digital advertising.

Paysafe is a global payments company providing merchant acquiring, digital wallets such as Skrill and NETELLER, and the pay-by-voucher paysafecard, along with ecommerce and iGaming payments. Customers are online merchants, gaming operators and consumers, with revenue about $1.7 billion. Headquartered in London, with major operations in Europe and North America. Listed on NYSE (PSFE) since 2021 after a SPAC merger with Foley Trasimene Acquisition Corp II. Known in online gaming and eSports payments.

Nuvei is a Montreal-based global payments technology company offering payment processing, acquiring, local payment methods, risk tools and card issuing for merchants in e-commerce, iGaming, travel and retail, in over 200 markets. Founded in 2003 by Philip Fayer. It went public on Nasdaq and TSX (NVEI) in 2021 and was taken private by Advent International in 2024 in a deal valued around $6.3 billion. Revenue was about $1.2 billion. B2B payments brand, notable in gaming and sports betting, with little consumer awareness.

Flywire is a Boston-based global payments enablement and software company, helping universities, healthcare providers, travel and B2B businesses collect cross-border and complex payments such as tuition and medical bills. Revenue comes from payment fees and software. Founded in 2009 as peerTransfer, with customers in over 140 countries and revenue of about $500 million. Listed on Nasdaq (FLYW) since 2021. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Ledger is a Paris-based maker of hardware wallets such as the Ledger Nano and Stax devices for storing cryptocurrency, plus the Ledger Live app and enterprise custody tools, having sold over 6 million devices. Founded in 2014. Customers are individual crypto holders and institutions. Has raised about $577 million in total funding and was valued over $1 billion. Private. Well-known crypto consumer brand, subject of a 2020 customer data leak.

International Money Express (Intermex) is a Miami-based remittance company that sends money from the US and Europe to Latin America and the Caribbean, mainly Mexico and Guatemala, through agent locations and a digital app. Customers are immigrant workers and their families, with revenue of about $650 million from fees and currency spreads. Listed on Nasdaq (IMXI). Western Union agreed in 2025 to acquire it. Well known among its target community.

PPRO is a London-based fintech providing payments infrastructure that lets global merchants and payment companies accept local payment methods, including e-wallets and bank transfers, in more than 100 markets via a single integration. Customers are payment service providers and large online merchants, with revenue from processing fees. Crunchbase shows about $463 million in funding. Private, backed by Citi and other investors. B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

about: Nayax is an Israeli fintech providing cashless payment, telemetry and management solutions for unattended retail such as vending machines, kiosks, car washes, laundromats and EV chargers, with card readers and a software platform deployed on millions of devices worldwide. Headquartered in Herzliya, with revenue of about $400 million. Listed on Nasdaq (NYAX) and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. B2B brand, though its readers are visible in public spaces.

Perfios is an Indian B2B fintech software company providing data aggregation, bank statement analysis, income verification, onboarding and credit decisioning tools to banks, lenders and fintechs in India and abroad, after acquiring Karza Technologies. Headquartered in Bangalore. Founded in 2008, with investors including Warburg Pincus and Kedaara Capital, and valued over $1 billion. Crunchbase shows about $441 million in funding. Private. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Backflip is an Austin, Texas proptech fintech offering software and financing for real estate investors who buy and renovate properties, with tools for deal analysis, renovation planning and lending. Customers are residential investors and flippers across the US. Crunchbase shows about $344 million in funding, including debt capital. Private. B2B niche brand with little general consumer awareness.

about: CMC Markets is a London-based online trading company offering contracts for difference, spread betting and forex through its Next Generation platform, plus stockbroking, and providing white-label technology to banks and brokers. Customers are retail and institutional traders in the UK, Europe, Australia and Asia. Founded in 1989. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (CMCX). Known among traders, and a past sponsor of sports and events.

re:cap is a Berlin-based capital operating system that combines debt and equity financing tools for startups and small businesses, including revenue-based financing, with a platform for managing funding. Customers are startups and scaleups, mainly in Europe. Crunchbase shows about $377 million in funding, largely debt facilities. Private. B2B fintech brand, known in the startup funding scene, with little consumer awareness.

about: Thunes is a Singapore-based cross-border payments network connecting banks, mobile money wallets and payment providers across more than 130 countries, letting customers send money to wallets, accounts and cards in real time. Customers are fintechs, remittance firms and global platforms, with revenue from transaction fees. Founded in 2016. Crunchbase shows about $352 million in funding. Private. B2B infrastructure brand, no consumer awareness.

Fibe, formerly EarlySalary, is a Pune-based Indian consumer lending app offering salary advances, personal loans and credit lines to young salaried professionals, using alternative data for credit decisions. Founded in 2015. Revenue comes from interest and fees on loans, with funding from investors such as TPG, Eight Roads and Ribbit. Crunchbase shows about $294 million raised. Private. Known fintech app in India, with consumer advertising.

Flow Traders is an Amsterdam-based technology-driven liquidity provider and market maker, trading exchange-traded products (ETFs and ETPs), equities, fixed income and crypto assets on global venues. Customers are exchanges, issuers and institutions, with revenue from trading gains and spreads of several hundred million euros. Founded in 2004. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (FLOW). B2B, with low retail awareness.

Flowdesk is a Paris-based digital asset trading company providing market making, liquidity, over-the-counter trading and treasury services to crypto projects, exchanges and institutions, using algorithmic strategies. Founded in 2020. Customers are token issuers and exchanges. Crunchbase shows about $282 million in funding, which likely includes capital for trading. Private. B2B brand known in the crypto industry, with no consumer awareness.

Revenue comes from swap fees and other services. Has raised about $268 million and was valued around $3 billion in 2025. Private. Large user base with strong awareness in the crypto community.

about: Istanbul-based Turkish bank founded in 1944, one of the country's largest private lenders, offering retail, SME, corporate and private banking through hundreds of branches and the World credit-card programme. Controlled by Koc Holding, with UniCredit having sold its stake. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (YKBNK). Strong consumer banking brand in Turkey with football and cultural sponsorship, but little international profile. Its customers include millions of retail and business clients in Turkey, with a strong credit-card franchise.

Atlanta-based regulated crypto and fintech platform, listed on the NYSE (BKKT), providing crypto custody, trading and loyalty-rewards infrastructure to banks, brokers and merchants. Created by Intercontinental Exchange in 2018 and went public through a SPAC in 2021. Customers are mostly B2B partners rather than consumers. Brand recognition is limited and concentrated in fintech and crypto circles. It was formed to develop a regulated platform for digital assets and has worked with large companies such as Starbucks on rewards.

Mexico City-based fintech lender (Konfio), founded 2013, offering credit lines, business credit cards and payments to small and mid-sized Mexican businesses. Backed by SoftBank, Goldman Sachs and others, valued around $1.3 billion at its peak. Customers are SMEs. Known in Mexican business circles, with limited broader consumer awareness. Konfio has a few thousand business customers and sells credit lines and payments tools through its app.

Toronto-based Canadian life insurer and wealth manager, founded 1865, selling insurance, retirement and asset management to individuals, employers and institutions in Canada, the US, Asia and the UK, with about $1.4 trillion in assets. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (SLF). Well-known consumer brand in Canada and sponsor of sports and cultural events. Sun Life has about 55,000 employees and operates in Canada, the US, Asia and the UK, with assets of about C$1.5 trillion.

Stockholm-based Swedish bank, founded 1871, providing retail and corporate banking in Sweden, the UK, Norway, Denmark and Finland through a branch-driven model and one of Europe's strongest credit ratings. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SHB A). Well known in Nordic markets, though with a conservative, low-profile marketing approach. The bank has around 12,000 staff and about 460 branches, and its customers include households and businesses.

Mumbai-based housing finance company, founded 2015, providing affordable home loans to low-income and informal-sector borrowers in smaller Indian cities. Backed by Kedaara Capital and others and listed in India (VASTU). Consumer-lending business with regional brand recognition rather than national visibility. Serves households in smaller cities, with loans secured on property. It has branches across several Indian states and focuses on first-time borrowers with informal incomes.

New York-based wealth management software company, founded 2009, providing the Addepar platform for aggregating, analysing and reporting portfolio data for wealth managers, family offices and institutions. Valued at about $3.25 billion after 2025 funding. B2B finance technology brand with strong visibility among advisers but little consumer awareness. Addepar employs about 1,000 people and manages trillions of dollars in assets on its platform.

Emerging Africa and Asia Infrastructure Fund (EAAIF) is a UK-managed public-private infrastructure financing fund, backed by development finance institutions and private investors, lending to infrastructure projects in Africa and Asia. The input lists London and $819 million of funding. B2B, no consumer visibility. Investors include governments and development finance institutions, and borrowers are infrastructure project companies. The fund is managed by Ninety One and was set up to finance infrastructure in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, with a focus on power and transport.
